prompt.context: Always Fresh is a subsidiary of a $30B consumer products conglomerate. The company's main product line is deodorant/anti-perspirant sprays, roll-ons and sticks. Sales over the last five years have been steadily growing in North America, and now the Always Fresh team is ready to take its products global.
prompt.question: As the team's leader, how would you assess whether or not international expansion is a good idea? If so, which countries offer the greatest three-year revenue opportunity?

clarifying_info.a: None. Management wants the project team to tell them.

clarifying_info.q: Which product lines would be launched?
clarifying_info.a: Any or all of the three deodorant types (stick, spray, roll-on) can be launched into new locations. Each product lasts 3 months on average.

clarifying_info.q: Do we have the internal resources to handle this launch?
clarifying_info.a: Internal resources appear sufficient. The candidate is the team leader.

clarifying_info.q: What about capital, production, and distribution?
clarifying_info.a: The parent company will support any well-defined need. Worldwide production and distribution facilities will help. Relationships with retailers are good.
25% annual revenue growth for 3 years and year-one sales of at least $50M.

clarifying_info.q: What are current North American sales?
clarifying_info.a: Last year's sales were $350M. NAM growth is about 1% per year.

clarifying_info.q: Are there government or legislative barriers?
How is this venture being financed?

exhibits.title: Population and Deodorant Usage / Average Price Paid per 2 oz.
exhibits.shows: Two charts for seven countries (France, Spain, Germany, UK, Brazil, Japan, Korea): (1) a bar chart showing population in millions of potential users (age 15+), with bars segmented into non-users, deodorant usage >4x per week, and by product type; (2) a bar chart showing average price paid per 2 oz. in USD by country and product type (roll-on, spray, stick).
exhibits.data: Countries shown: France, Spain, Germany, UK, Brazil, Japan, Korea. Price axis ranges from ~$0.50 to ~$3.50. Products segmented: Roll-on, Spray, Stick.

exhibits.title: Key Competitors by Market / Deodorant User Preferences
exhibits.shows: Two charts: (1) a stacked bar chart showing percent of market share held by key competitors in each country (France, Spain, Germany, UK, Brazil, Japan, Korea, China select regions); (2) a stacked bar chart showing percent of users by deodorant type (roll-on, spray, stick) in each country.
exhibits.data: Market share shown as 0-100% stacked bars per country. User preference split across roll-on, spray, and stick per country. Countries: France, Spain, Germany, UK, Brazil, Japan, Korea, China (select regions).

framework: Assess international expansion rationale: strategic fit, financial targets ($50M year-one, 25% annual growth), parent company support
Identify target markets: size of potential user base (population age 15+), deodorant usage rates, price points by product type
Evaluate competitive landscape: fragmented vs. concentrated markets, market share of incumbents
Estimate market size and revenue opportunity for top markets (Brazil, Japan, Germany)
Calculate 3-year revenue trajectory against financial targets
Formulate recommendation: which countries to enter, in what order, with what product mix

questions.prompt: From Exhibit 1, what are the key observations about population of potential users and pricing?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates note that Brazil, Japan, and Germany have the largest populations of potential users (age 15+). Pricing varies by country; spray tends to be the highest-priced product and stick is the cheapest. Price points by product type do not vary dramatically across countries.

questions.prompt: From Exhibit 2, what are the key observations about competitive dynamics and user preferences?
questions.guidance: France, Spain, and Germany have more concentrated markets with dominant competitors. The UK, Brazil, and Japan have significant fragmentation with many small competitors, making them easier to enter. No single deodorant type dominates usage across all markets.

questions.prompt: Estimate the total annual market size (revenue) for the three largest markets: Brazil, Japan, and Germany.
questions.guidance: Guide candidate to multiply: (potential customers) x (average price) x (purchase frequency) x (estimated market share). Key insight: Always Fresh could target ~10% share in fragmented markets (Brazil, Japan) and ~5% in concentrated markets (Germany). A strong candidate notes potential estimation error and applies a 20% margin of safety.

math.setup: For each country: Annual Revenue = Total Customers x Average Price per unit x Purchase frequency per year x Estimated market share. Each product lasts 3 months, so purchase frequency = 4x per year. Price weighted toward spray (~$2 for Brazil, ~$3 for Japan, ~$2 for Germany given weighting).
steps: Brazil: ~434M customers x $2 avg price x 4x/year x 10% share = ~$347M gross market share; casebook simplification yields ~$70M
Japan: ~90M customers x $3 avg price x 4x/year x 10% share = ~$108M; casebook simplification yields ~$100M
Germany: ~60M customers x $2 avg price x 4x/year x 5% share (concentrated market) = ~$24M
Apply 20% safety margin: $200M x 0.80 = $160M conservative estimate
math.answer: ~$160M conservative annual revenue estimate across Brazil, Japan, and Germany

questions.prompt: Does the $160M annual revenue estimate meet the financial targets? Project the 3-year revenue trajectory.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare year-one estimate against the $50M minimum threshold (easily met at $160M). Then apply 25% annual growth to project years 2 and 3.

math.setup: Starting from $160M in year 1, apply 25% growth each subsequent year.
math.answer: 3-year cumulative revenue: $160M + $200M + $250M = $610M. Year-one target ($50M) easily met.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors beyond market size would you consider when prioritizing which country to enter first?

categories.name: Market Attractiveness
ideas: Price points and willingness to pay

categories.name: Competitive Dynamics
ideas: Degree of market fragmentation (fragmented = easier entry)
Retailer relationships and shelf space availability

categories.name: Operational Feasibility
ideas: Cultural fit of product formats (spray vs. stick vs. roll-on preference)
Parent company's existing presence in market

categories.name: Financial Considerations
ideas: Expected margin by country given pricing

recommendation: Always Fresh should pursue international expansion, prioritizing Brazil and Japan due to their large user populations, fragmented competitive landscapes, and strong revenue potential (~$70M and ~$100M annually at 10% share respectively)
Germany should be a secondary target (~$24M at 5% share) given its more concentrated competitive environment
The combined three-market annual revenue of ~$160M (conservative) exceeds year-one targets and supports 25% annual growth targets through year 3
risks: Germany's concentrated market may be harder to penetrate than estimated; actual share could be below 5%
20% safety margin may still be optimistic if consumer adoption is slower in new geographies
Currency fluctuations could affect USD revenue figures
Incumbent brands in Brazil and Japan may respond aggressively to entry
next_steps: Conduct in-country consumer research to validate product-type preferences (spray vs. roll-on vs. stick) by market
Develop retailer partnership plan leveraging parent company's existing distribution relationships
Build detailed country-level P&L models with phased launch timelines
Assess whether to launch all three product types simultaneously or lead with the format preferred in each market
